concepts.why: The patient's grade III diastolic dysfunction and biatrial dilatation are indicative of diastolic dysfunction.
The patient's history of metastatic bladder carcinoma is a significant finding that needs to be considered in the differential diagnosis.
The patient's history of pulmonary tuberculosis treated with antituberculous therapy is a relevant finding that may be contributing to the patient's current symptoms.
The patient's diastolic dysfunction and biatrial dilatation, in combination with the history of metastatic bladder carcinoma, raise the possibility of cardiac amyloidosis.
The patient's irregular narrow complex tachycardia with a ventricular rate of 78 bpm and atrial rate of 210 bpm is also consistent with atrial flutter.
The patient's prominent y descent and biatrial dilatation, in combination with the history of pulmonary tuberculosis, raise the possibility of constrictive pericarditis.
The patient's diastolic dysfunction and biatrial dilatation, in combination with the history of metastatic bladder carcinoma, also raise the possibility of restrictive cardiomyopathy.
It explains the prolonged P-wave duration of 160 milliseconds.
